passage.text: Every Thai student knows the name Sunthorn Phu.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈtaɪ ˈstuːdənt ˈnoʊz ðə ˈneɪm ˈsʊntɔːrn ˈpuː.

passage.text: He is Thailand's most famous poet, and his birthday, June 26, is Sunthorn Phu Day in Thai schools.
passage.reading: hiː ɪz ˈtaɪlændz ˈmoʊst ˈfeɪməs ˈpoʊɪt, ənd hɪz ˈbɜːrθdeɪ, ˈdʒuːn ˈtwɛnti ˈsɪks, ɪz ˈsʊntɔːrn ˈpuː ˈdeɪ ɪn ˈtaɪ ˈskuːlz.

passage.text: He was born in Bangkok in 1786 and grew up near a royal palace, where his mother worked.
passage.reading: hiː wʌz ˈbɔːrn ɪn ˈbæŋkɑːk ɪn ˈsɛvəntiːn ˈeɪti ˈsɪks ənd ˈɡruː ˈʌp ˈnɪr ə ˈrɔɪəl ˈpæləs, wɛr hɪz ˈmʌðər ˈwɜːrkt.

passage.text: As a young man, he loved writing poems, and people soon noticed his talent.
passage.reading: əz ə ˈjʌŋ ˈmæn, hiː ˈlʌvd ˈraɪtɪŋ ˈpoʊəmz, ənd ˈpiːpəl ˈsuːn ˈnoʊtɪst hɪz ˈtælənt.

passage.text: King Rama II, who also wrote poems, invited him to work at the palace as a royal poet.
passage.reading: ˈkɪŋ ˈrɑːmə ðə ˈsɛkənd, huː ˈɔːlsoʊ ˈroʊt ˈpoʊəmz, ɪnˈvaɪtɪd hɪm tə ˈwɜːrk ət ðə ˈpæləs əz ə ˈrɔɪəl ˈpoʊɪt.

passage.text: But after the king passed away in 1824, Sunthorn Phu lost his job, and his life became difficult.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈæftər ðə ˈkɪŋ ˈpæst əˈweɪ ɪn ˈeɪtiːn ˈtwɛnti ˈfɔːr, ˈsʊntɔːrn ˈpuː ˈlɔːst hɪz ˈdʒɑːb, ənd hɪz ˈlaɪf bɪˈkeɪm ˈdɪfɪkəlt.

passage.text: He became a monk and traveled around the country for many years.
passage.reading: hiː bɪˈkeɪm ə ˈmʌŋk ənd ˈtrævəld əˈraʊnd ðə ˈkʌntri fər ˈmɛni ˈjɪrz.

passage.text: On his journeys, he wrote poems about the places he saw and the people he missed.
passage.reading: ɑːn hɪz ˈdʒɜːrniz, hiː ˈroʊt ˈpoʊəmz əˈbaʊt ðə ˈpleɪsɪz hiː ˈsɔː ənd ðə ˈpiːpəl hiː ˈmɪst.

passage.text: His masterpiece is Phra Aphai Mani, a very long poem about a hero who travels across the sea.
passage.reading: hɪz ˈmæstərpiːs ɪz ˈprɑː ˈɑːpaɪ ˈmɑːni, ə ˈvɛri ˈlɔːŋ ˈpoʊəm əˈbaʊt ə ˈhɪroʊ huː ˈtrævəlz əˈkrɔːs ðə ˈsiː.

passage.text: It took him about twenty years to write it.
passage.reading: ɪt ˈtʊk hɪm əˈbaʊt ˈtwɛnti ˈjɪrz tə ˈraɪt ɪt.

passage.text: Sunthorn Phu passed away in 1855, at the age of sixty-nine.
passage.reading: ˈsʊntɔːrn ˈpuː ˈpæst əˈweɪ ɪn ˈeɪtiːn ˈfɪfti ˈfaɪv, ət ði ˈeɪdʒ əv ˈsɪksti ˈnaɪn.

passage.text: In 1986, two hundred years after his birth, UNESCO named him one of the world's great poets.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈnaɪntiːn ˈeɪti ˈsɪks, ˈtuː ˈhʌndrəd ˈjɪrz ˈæftər hɪz ˈbɜːrθ, juːˈnɛskoʊ ˈnɑːmd hɪm ˈwʌn əv ðə ˈwɜːrldz ˈɡreɪt ˈpoʊɪts.

passage.text: Today, Thai children still read his poems and memorize them.
passage.reading: təˈdeɪ, ˈtaɪ ˈtʃɪldrən ˈstɪl ˈriːd hɪz ˈpoʊəmz ənd ˈmɛməraɪz ˈðɛm.
